clue.text: Source of apple juice with high priority

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, so take its opening letter

parts.note: sap is the juice of a plant

explanation.surface: Apple juice from the source is treated as urgent business.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation for 'as soon as possible' marks a task given top priority.

clue.text: A little gadget, which shows when you've stopped

definitions.text: A little gadget, which shows when you've stopped

parts.words: A little gadget, which shows when you've stopped
parts.note: a dashboard dial, named in a clipped casual form, whose needle sits at nought once the car halts; the surface also hints at skimpy swimwear

explanation.surface: A tiny device that lights up when you finally stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little' tells you the word is a shortened form: the dashboard dial is a speedometer, and when you stop it shows nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal short name for a speedometer, the instrument whose needle sits at zero when the car stands still.

clue.text: Advanced position for hide: badger annihilated

indicators.note: something annihilated is smashed to bits, so these letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A forward camp chosen as a hide after the badger was wiped out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'annihilated' rearranges the letters of HIDE and BADGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A military foothold won on the enemy's side of a river, the furthest point an army has pushed forward.

clue.text: Old wife's tale told of Big Apple

indicators.note: something told is spoken, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: an old wife is a ..., and her tale is a myth, giving a ... myth

explanation.surface: An old wives' tale about New York, the Big Apple.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'granny's myth' sounds like the apple variety. 'Big Apple' looks like New York but defines a large green apple.
explanation.definitionFit: A Granny Smith is a large, sharp green variety of eating and cooking apple.

clue.text: Of course, part is in apple-pie order

definitions.meaning: a racecourse has a long level section, the run-in or back stretch
neat and tidy, everything set right

explanation.definitionFit: A straight is the level stretch of a racecourse, and things put straight are in apple-pie order, neatly arranged.

clue.text: Apple product paid off

indicators.note: something gone off has been spoiled, so these four letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: An Apple gadget that has been paid off in full.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges the letters of PAID.
explanation.definitionFit: Apple's tablet computer is one of the firm's best-known products.

clue.text: Dried food? It's apple crumble

indicators.note: to crumble is to break into pieces, so these letters are broken and remade

explanation.surface: A dessert of dried fruit: it's apple crumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumble' rearranges the letters of IT'S and APPLE.
explanation.definitionFit: These halved dried pulses are a store-cupboard food used for soups such as pease pudding.

clue.text: First 11 letters of "skunk"

parts.note: the opening eleven letters of the alphabet are named by their first and last, joined by a word for 'up to', and the phrase also echoes a puff of cannabis

explanation.walkthrough: The entry names the alphabet's first eleven letters as a range from its first letter to its eleventh; said aloud it is close to 'a toke' of skunk, a potent strain of cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: The alphabet's opening eleven letters span from its first letter to its eleventh, which is K.

clue.text: Arrest pub-crawling wild child

indicators.note: a pub crawl wanders from bar to bar, so these letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Police arrest a badly behaved youngster on a pub crawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crawling' rearranges the letters of ARREST and PUB.
explanation.definitionFit: A badly behaved young celebrity, a term coined for tantrum-throwing tennis players, is a wild child.

clue.text: Part of Apple Computers gets the bird

parts.note: a pip is the seed inside an apple's core
IT, information technology, is computing

explanation.surface: A division of Apple's computer business is given the bird, booed off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets the bird' sounds like being jeered; here the bird is the definition, a small songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipit is a small brown songbird of open country, a kind of bird.

clue.text: An apple a day keeps this, I pray

indicators.note: the phrase holds the word within it, keeping it inside its letters

explanation.surface: The old saying about an apple a day, recited as a prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps this' says the answer sits inside 'apple a day', across its words.
explanation.definitionFit: To pray in the old sense is to beg or entreat, which is a synonym.

clue.text: On the rocks? Not in this case, though sadly taken in about doctor

definitions.text: On the rocks? Not in this case

indicators.note: about means around, so the jumbled letters surround the other piece
sadly suggests something gone wrong, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A drink on ice, sadly swallowed by a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'on the rocks' as served with ice: a neat drink is the case where that does not happen, so the whole question is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirits drunk without ice or mixer are the opposite of a drink served on the rocks.

clue.text: Apple (Pink Lady) the ultimate for baking etc

parts.note: a cooker is an apple grown for cooking rather than eating

indicators.note: ultimate means last, so take the closing letter of the variety's name

explanation.surface: A Pink Lady apple being the very best fruit for baking.
explanation.walkthrough: Pink Lady is an eating apple, so it looks like the apple; it only supplies its last letter, while 'Apple' gives a cooking apple.
explanation.definitionFit: Cookery is the craft of preparing food, which includes baking, roasting and the rest.

clue.text: Multifunctional tool for haircare by Boatman

parts.note: a comb is a tool for tidying hair
the setter calls himself Boatman, so he is I

explanation.surface: The setter offers a multi-purpose grooming gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: A combi is a combination appliance, like a combi boiler, doing several jobs at once.

clue.text: On the rocks and abandoned, could be Apple follower

indicators.note: abandoned means given up, so the letters of the little word are dropped

parts.note: a ship on the rocks has run aground
taken as written, its letters scattered through the other word
apple is one kind of pie

explanation.surface: Stranded and deserted, perhaps a fan of the Apple brand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' takes the A, N and D of AND out of AGROUND, leaving GROU.
explanation.definitionFit: A groupie is a devoted fan who follows a band about, a follower.

clue.text: Bilious? So try sweet seafood dish

indicators.note: a bilious stomach is upset, so these letters are churned around

explanation.surface: Feeling queasy? Then try a sweet dish of seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bilious' rearranges the letters of SO TRY SWEET.
explanation.definitionFit: Oyster stew is a creamy dish of oysters simmered in milk, a seafood dish.

clue.text: The Eagles, reformed, endorse absent party

indicators.note: a reformed band has regrouped, so the remaining letters are set in a new order
absent means missing, so the party's letters are taken out

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: The rock band the Eagles reunite but back a party that doesn't show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absent' removes DO from ENDORSE, leaving ENRSE, which 'reformed' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernes are sea eagles, so the plural stands for the eagles of the clue.

clue.text: Might have an Apple? I hardly think so!

definitions.meaning: a person's pupil, the apple of the eye, sits in an eye such as this one

explanation.definitionFit: My eye may hold the apple of my eye, and 'my eye!' is an old cry of disbelief.

clue.text: In transport in the City and not moving

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London
static means still

explanation.surface: Stuck in transport in the City and going nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In transport' reads as travel; it means carried away with joy.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in transport is to be overcome with delight, which is being rapturous.

clue.text: See 27
Gander with citrus sliced over big apple

indicators.note: in a down clue over puts one piece above the next
sliced fruit is cut up, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: the Big Apple is New York, abbreviated NY

explanation.surface: A goose with sliced citrus served over a large apple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gander' looks like the male goose; it is a look at something.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a gander is British slang for having a look, and scrutiny is a close look.

clue.text: Boatman gives away an apple for a lover

indicators.note: giving something away means losing it, so these letters are removed

parts.note: a coxswain steers a rowing boat
Cox's Orange Pippin is an apple, called a Cox

explanation.surface: The setter, Boatman, gives his beloved an apple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boatman' looks like the setter's name but is a coxswain; removing the Cox apple leaves the lover.
explanation.definitionFit: A swain is a poetic word for a young male suitor, a lover.

clue.text: Popular Apple product: they say dealing with it is wrong

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: what people say is heard, so the drink's name stands for its sound

parts.note: cider is a drink made from apples

explanation.surface: A popular Apple gadget is said to be bad to deal with.
explanation.walkthrough: Insider dealing is illegal trading on secret knowledge, so the definition describes the term cryptically.
explanation.definitionFit: Trading shares on private knowledge is called insider dealing, a crime in most markets.

clue.text: Apple product reported for bugs

indicators.note: reported means spoken of, so the band's name is heard aloud

parts.note: the Beatles recorded on their own Apple label

explanation.surface: An Apple product said to be full of bugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apple product' suggests a computer; it is the band on Apple Records.
explanation.definitionFit: Beetles are insects, and in loose speech any insect is a bug.

clue.text: "The Graduate" offends in scenes of depression

parts.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts graduate
to sin is to offend

explanation.surface: The hero of the film The Graduate offends in gloomy scenes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Graduate' looks like the film, and 'depression' like low mood; here it means hollows in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A basin is a hollow in the land, so basins are sites of depression in the geographic sense.

clue.text: Clue to dial home — with a bad back?

parts.note: in a down light, the word read upwards spells the clue word dial

explanation.surface: A hint for ringing home when your back has given out.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as wordplay, LAID written UP in a down grid becomes DIAL, so the answer is a clue to that word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone confined to bed by illness or injury, such as a bad back, is said to be out of action.

clue.text: Friends prepared girl on mountain retreat

indicators.note: to retreat is to go back, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: set means ready or prepared
Amy is a girl's name
an alp is a mountain

explanation.surface: Friends got a girl ready for a mountain retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' turns SET, AMY and ALP back to front together.
explanation.definitionFit: Playmates are childhood companions, friends to play with.

clue.text: Fruit, the first apple …

parts.note: a pear is a fruit
main means chief, first in importance

explanation.surface: Fruit: first of all an apple, and the clue runs on.
explanation.definitionFit: The pearmain is an old English variety of apple.

clue.text: See 24
See 4
… provides clue for confused, hesitant leader of England dropped

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the remaining letters are jumbled
dropped means let go, so one letter is removed
a leader goes first, so take the opening letter

explanation.surface: A muddled, hesitant English leader is dropped, and that gives a clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader of England' is E; 'dropped' takes it out of HESITANT, and 'confused' rearranges HSITANT.
explanation.definitionFit: To hint at something is to give a clue to it, as a suggestion rather than a statement.

clue.text: Excuse for unnatural sex act involving movement of women, perhaps

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so one piece is wrapped round the other

parts.note: AI, artificial insemination, is conception without the usual act
women's lib, the women's liberation movement

explanation.surface: A sordid excuse involving a sex act and feminist activists.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim of being elsewhere, used loosely for any excuse.

clue.text: Runner not deviating from one direction

indicators.note: deviating means straying from the path, so these letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A runner who never strays from one direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deviating' rearranges RUNNER and NOT; a non-return valve lets fluid flow one way only.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-return valve permits flow in one direction alone, so the term describes one-way travel.
